summary: Iteration 3 — verified GridFS upload/serve, runtime SEO patch, eye-toggles, bulk reorder, and full regression. 35/36 backend pytest pass; the one failure is a real CRITICAL deployment bug — request.base_url returns the internal cluster hostname/scheme (http://aniket-interiors.cluster-5.preview.emergentcf.cloud) instead of what the user actually hit (https://aniket-interiors.preview.emergentagent.com), which breaks portfolio image rendering on the public admin UI due to mixed-content blocking.

critical.issue: Returned `url` uses the INTERNAL proxy host and `http://` scheme (e.g. http://aniket-interiors.cluster-5.preview.emergentcf.cloud/api/uploads/<id>) instead of the public https URL the browser is on. Browsers will block these as mixed content when shown on https admin pages, and the URL won't even resolve from outside Cloudflare's edge. This DEFEATS the purpose of the iteration's 'auto-detect domain at runtime'. Fix: either start uvicorn with `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'` in /etc/supervisor/conf.d/supervisord.conf, OR change `_abs_base()` in server.py to read X-Forwarded-Proto / X-Forwarded-Host headers explicitly (e.g. scheme = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-proto', request.url.scheme); host = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-host', request.url.netloc)). Current uvicorn cmd: `uvicorn server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --workers 1 --reload` — missing --proxy-headers.

minor.issue: Backend correctly sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, but Cloudflare edge rewrites it to `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` on the public URL. Verified via direct localhost:8001 hit that backend header is correct — this is an infra/edge concern, not a code bug. Document or align with platform team if long caching is desired.

action_items: FIX CRITICAL: Make /api/admin/upload return the public scheme/host. Easiest fix — add `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'` to the uvicorn command in /etc/supervisor/conf.d/supervisord.conf and `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. Alternatively patch `_abs_base(request)` in server.py to honour X-Forwarded-Proto/Host. Without this, any image uploaded via the admin UI on the deployed site will appear broken (mixed-content / wrong-host).
Same `_abs_base()` is also used to build the password-reset link in send_reset_email — the email currently sends an http:// cluster URL too. Same fix resolves both.
critical_code_review_comments: _abs_base() trusts request.base_url which behind Cloudflare/ingress reflects the internal hop, not the user-facing URL. Use forwarded headers.

GridFS upload metadata stores content_type but serve_upload pulls it via grid_out.metadata.get; if metadata is missing (e.g. legacy file), defaults to application/octet-stream — fine, but gridfs.open_download_stream raises NoFile for missing IDs which is swallowed by a broad `except Exception`; consider catching gridfs.errors.NoFile specifically so a real I/O error doesn't get masked as 404.

ALLOWED_IMAGE_EXT does not validate magic-bytes — a file named .png with arbitrary bytes is accepted. Low risk since served with content-type derived from extension, but consider Pillow.Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)).verify() for hardening.
bulk_write reorder: no validation that supplied ids actually exist; non-existent ids are silently no-op (UpdateOne matched_count=0). Acceptable but logging count mismatch would help debugging.

GridFS files have no orphan-cleanup — when a portfolio item is deleted, the underlying GridFS file remains. Consider a cleanup hook in admin_delete_portfolio that extracts the ObjectId from the stored image_url and calls gridfs.delete().
PasswordField uses inline styles instead of Tailwind utility classes; consistent enough but worth aligning with the rest of the codebase eventually.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — added GridFS-specific tests (id is 24-char hex, url ends with /api/uploads/<id>, 404 cases for invalid+nonexistent ids, runtime SEO patch script, public-https proxy URL assertion, localhost base_url adaptation); split content-type check from cache-control (Cloudflare overrides cache-control on the public URL).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (eye-toggles: login + reset (2 fields) + settings (4 fields) + SEO runtime URL patch all verified live)

context_for_next_testing_agent: ONE outstanding bug: TestUpload::test_upload_url_uses_public_https_when_proxied fails because request.base_url reflects the internal cluster hostname/scheme. Once the main agent adds --proxy-headers to uvicorn (or patches _abs_base to use X-Forwarded-* headers), this test will pass and so will the same issue in the password-reset email link. Note: test_upload_image_ok asserts content-type and Cache-Control separately — Cache-Control is verified at localhost:8001 (Cloudflare strips it on the public hop). Frontend splash screen takes ~2.5-3s before the form renders — Playwright tests should wait_for_timeout(3500) before querying admin form testids.
rca_of_the_issue: _abs_base(request) returns str(request.base_url) which Starlette derives from the ASGI scope's `scheme` and `headers[host]`. When uvicorn is NOT started with --proxy-headers, it ignores X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host and uses the raw TCP connection scheme (http) and the literal Host header arriving from the ingress (the cluster hostname, not the user-facing one). Result: returned URL is http://internal-cluster/.../ which (a) is mixed content on the https admin page → browser blocks rendering, and (b) is not the canonical user URL. Mitigation: append `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'` to the uvicorn command, OR replace _abs_base with: `scheme = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-proto') or request.url.scheme; host = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-host') or request.url.netloc; return f'{scheme}://{host}'`.
